questions.q: Profiles 1/1/1 are active. What does `diff` without arguments print in INAV 9.1.0?
options: Only the `master` section, without a single profile — profiles are printed by `diff all`
The `master` section and one active profile of each kind
The `master` section and all 3 + 2 + 3 profiles
Only the settings changed since the last `save`
questions.explain: In `printConfig()` with the `DUMP_MASTER` mask the branch “dump just the current profiles” is executed: master and the active control, mixer and battery profile are printed. All profiles and `defaults noreboot` come only from `diff all`.

questions.q: How many profile selection commands (`control_profile N`, `mixer_profile N`, `battery_profile N`) are in the `diff all` of an H743 board with INAV 9.1.0?
questions.explain: There are 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 blocks, each preceded by its own selection command; at the end three more lines restore the original selection: 8 + 3 = 11. An F411 has one mixer profile, so there it is 7 + 3 = 10.

questions.q: A file starts with `batch start`. On paste two lines gave `### ERROR: Invalid name`. What does the first `save` do?
options: Refuses, prints the number of errors and resets batch mode
Saves everything except the two lines and reboots the board
Rolls the configuration back to the state before the paste and reboots
Saves the configuration but leaves the `SETTINGFAIL` flag until it is fixed
questions.explain: With an active batch that has errors `cliSave()` prints “N ERRORS WERE DETECTED” and “PLEASE FIX ERRORS THEN 'SAVE'”, resets the batch and returns without writing. A second `save` will write — which is exactly why you must not type it without fixing the file.

questions.q: You pasted a `diff all` with three control profiles, changed your mind and typed `exit`. Why did some settings change anyway?
options: `exit` in INAV saves the configuration just like `save`
`batch start` writes every line at once
The profile selection commands write EEPROM themselves when the number changes
`defaults noreboot` at the start of the file had already erased the old config in RAM
questions.explain: `control_profile`, `mixer_profile` and `battery_profile` call `set…ProfileAndWriteEEPROM`: on a change of index the current configuration is written. Only `defaults` and a restore from a backup undo such a paste.

questions.q: Which line from an INAV 8.0.1 `diff all` gives `### ERROR: Invalid name` in 9.1.0 and is NOT fixed by the migration file `8_to_9.json` of Configurator 9.1.0?
options: `set mixer_pid_profile_linking = ON`
`set controlrate_profile = 2`
`set osd_pan_servo_pwm2centideg = 18`
`set reboot_character = 114`
questions.explain: The migration file renames the first three names. `reboot_character` was removed in 9.0, and the `removed` list in `8_to_9.json` is empty — the line stays red and is deleted by hand.

questions.q: You saved a `diff all` from the CLI tab to a text file and gave it to the Restore Config button in Configurator 9.1. There is no migration window. Why?
options: Migration works only for auto-backups named `UPDATE_…`
The Configurator reads the version from the line `# INAV/<target> 8.0.1`, and it is commented out
Migration is enabled only when flashing without Full chip erase
The file has no `# Version: X.Y.Z` line, and the backup version was not recognized
questions.explain: `extractBackupVersion()` looks only for the pattern `# Version: …` from the header that the Configurator writes itself. Without it the migration chain is empty, and the file goes to the CLI as is.

questions.q: Which calibrations get into an INAV 9.1.0 `diff all`?
options: None: calibrations are stored separately from the settings and survive `defaults`
Only `vbat_scale` and `current_meter_scale`
The accelerometer, the compass, the gyro zeros, the voltage and current scales
Only the compass: `magzero_*` and `maggain_*`
questions.explain: `acczero_*`, `accgain_*`, `magzero_*`, `maggain_*`, `gyro_zero_*`, `vbat_scale`, `current_meter_*` are ordinary settings of the master section. That is why they must not be moved to another board.

questions.q: `status` showed `Arming disabled flags: NAV ARMSW CLI`. What do you do first?
options: Flip the arm switch several times — `ARMSW` is the most important of the three
Reflash the board: `NAV` means a failure of the navigation core
Leave the CLI and turn the arm switch off, then deal with `NAV`
Calibrate the compass and the accelerometer
questions.explain: `CLI` is set while the CLI is open. `ARMSW` appears when the switch is on during any other block and clears after it is turned off. `NAV` is left: no fix, a navigation mode is active or a mission error — an explanation is printed under the flag.

questions.q: Why is `dump all` worse than `diff all` as a file for moving to a new major version?
options: It does not contain the profiles, only master
It prints the settings in hexadecimal, and the CLI of the new version cannot parse them
It cannot be pasted into the CLI: the line format is different
It fixes all the old defaults in place and does not start with `defaults noreboot`
questions.explain: `dump` prints every setting, including those equal to the default: after a paste the new 9.x defaults are overwritten with the old ones. `defaults noreboot` is printed only with `diff all`. `docs/Cli.md` also advises restoring from a `diff`.

options: only shows which pin is used for what
reassigns the function of a pin, as in Betaflight
resets the timer assignments to the target defaults
shows free memory and the stack
questions.explain: `cliResource()` prints the pin table and takes no arguments. The output assignment is changed through `timer_output_mode` and the Mixer tab or with a custom target.
